relations.subject: index:index-pushdown
relations.evidence: The Query engine tries to leverage the indexer functionality as much as possible by pushing down operations to the indexer as part of the index scan.

relations.subject: index:index-pushdown

relations.subject: index-type:gsi

relations.subject: index:index-projection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - family membership; the page files this as its first Index Pushdowns section and describes it as data requested as part of the index-scan

relations.subject: index:index-projection
relations.evidence: For a covered query, it is the fields referred in projection, predicate, GROUP BY clauses, ORDER BY clauses, HAVING clauses, ON key, and subqueries of the query. For non-covered queries, it is just `META().id`.

relations.subject: index:index-projection

relations.evidence: If the `index_projection` field is missing in the EXPLAIN output, then Indexer would return all index-keys.

relations.subject: index:skip-key-range-scan
relations.evidence: it is possible to push down a composite predicate on non-continuous leading index-keys. There must be a predicate on the first key in the index definition, and then on any of the subsequent index-keys.

relations.subject: index:pagination-pushdown
relations.evidence: Pagination in SQL++ queries is achieved by using the LIMIT and OFFSET clauses, and both of the operators can be pushed to indexer whenever possible.

relations.subject: index:pagination-pushdown
relations.evidence: When using IntersectScan, the Query engine uses multiple indexes to process the query. As such, LIMIT/OFFSET will need to be processed in the Query engine at a later stage of query processing, and hence cannot be pushed to the Indexer.

relations.subject: index:pagination-pushdown
relations.evidence: When ORDER BY key in the query is different from that of the index order, then the query layer will need to process the sort; and hence, in those cases, the pagination cannot be pushed to the indexer

relations.subject: index:pagination-pushdown
relations.evidence: For JOIN queries, index scans can be used only for the left side keyspace. Subsequent JOIN phrases may filter some documents, after which only LIMIT/OFFSET can be applied. Hence, the pagination operators cannot be pushed when a query has JOIN clauses.

relations.subject: index:order-pushdown
relations.evidence: The Query engine may avoid ORDER BY processing in cases where the ordering of entries in the index can be leveraged for the query.

relations.subject: index:order-pushdown
relations.evidence: Currently the Query engine supports order pushdown only when the ORDER BY keys are aligned with the Index order. But reverse-scan of the index is not supported.

relations.subject: index:operator-pushdown
relations.evidence: The Query engine tries to avoid unnecessary processing operators such as MIN(), MAX(), and COUNT(), which can be processed by the Indexer much more efficiently. In such cases, the Query engine pushes down necessary hints or options to the Indexer to process the following operators.

notable_absence.finding: No pushdown on this page carries a version. Two paragraphs are written as if they did - 'In Couchbase Capella, the Query service and Indexer are enhanced with complete and accurate predicate pushdown...' and 'In Couchbase Capella, it is possible to push down a composite predicate on non-continuous leading index-keys' - where 'are enhanced' and 'it is possible' are the residue of a Server release note whose version has been deleted for the Capella edition. The word 'Currently' in the order-pushdown Limitation does the same job. So the family's members are undatable from this page, and any availableSince for them would have to come from the Server tree. A second absence worth phase 2's attention: the page names IntersectScan, distinctScan and intersectScan as the conditions that DEFEAT pagination pushdown and force primary-key retrieval, but never defines any of them and links nothing that does. Three of the five pages in this batch cite these scan operators as limitations; none of the five defines them. There is no `index:index-scan-operator` enum anywhere in the corpus, and there ought to be.

cross_component_finding: The pushdown family is spelled across two namespaces in the corpus, and this record reproduces the split rather than silently resolving it: the family (index:index-pushdown) and five of its members (index:index-projection, index:predicate-pushdown, index:pagination-pushdown, index:order-pushdown, index:operator-pushdown) are `index:`, but the two operator-pushdown members that already exist in the corpus are `n1ql:max-pushdown` and `n1ql:min-pushdown`, minted from the Server 7.2 sibling page. I reused those spellings and matched them when minting n1ql:count-pushdown and n1ql:count-distinct-pushdown, because forking MIN and MAX into a second namespace inside one record would be worse than an inconsistency I can flag. Phase 2 should pick one: the retired-prefixes guidance says `index:` is for pushdowns, which argues for index:min-pushdown / index:max-pushdown / index:count-pushdown / index:count-distinct-pushdown and an alias from the n1ql: spellings. Note the operator pushdowns are the only members named after SQL++ functions rather than after index mechanics, which is presumably why the earlier round reached for `n1ql:`.
cross_product_finding: This is the Capella copy of a page that also exists in the Server tree (server/7.2/learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/index_pushdowns), and the Capella copy has had its version markers stripped without having its sentences rewritten - 'In Couchbase Capella, the Query service and Indexer are enhanced with...' reads as a change announcement with no release to anchor it. The examples were also re-pointed at pre-installed travel-sample indexes ('This example uses the `def_inventory_route_route_src_dst_day` index that comes pre-installed'), which is a Capella-specific fact: on Server those indexes are not pre-installed. Any relation asserting index existence from this page is therefore Capella-only and must not be generalised to Server.
